project.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

parsed_output.patch_notes:
Applied the authoritative upstream security fix (codehaus-plexus/plexus-utils commit b38a1b3a43, "[PLXUTILS-161] Commandline shell injection problems") verbatim, adapted to this repo's pre-fix baseline (confirmed byte-identical to the upstream pre-fix revision for the three touched source files):

1. src/main/java/org/codehaus/plexus/util/cli/shell/Shell.java:
   - Added `unconditionallyQuote` flag + `setUnconditionalQuoting(boolean)`.
   - Added `quoteOneItem(String, boolean isExecutable)` helper that centralizes quoting/escaping via `StringUtils.quoteAndEscape(..., unconditionallyQuote)`.
   - `getRawCommandLine()` now calls `quoteOneItem(getOriginalExecutable(), true)` / `quoteOneItem(arg, false)` instead of inlining `StringUtils.quoteAndEscape` calls with `force=false`.
   - `getShellCommandLine()` now sources the executable via `getOriginalExecutable()` (the raw stored value) rather than the already-shell-munged `getExecutable()`, avoiding double processing.

2. src/main/java/org/codehaus/plexus/util/cli/shell/BourneShell.java:
   - Removed `BASH_QUOTING_TRIGGER_CHARS`/`getQuotingTriggerChars()` override — no longer needed because quoting is now unconditional.
   - Constructor calls `setUnconditionalQuoting(true)` and changed `setExecutableQuoteDelimiter` from `'"'` to `'\''` (single quote).
   - Replaced `unifyQuotes(String)` (double-quote wrap, escaped only the quote char) with `quoteOneItem(String, boolean)` that always single-quotes and replaces embedded `'` with the POSIX-safe `'"'"'` sequence — single-quoted content is fully inert to `$`, backticks, and backslashes, closing the command-substitution injection.
   - `getExecutable()` / `getExecutionPreamble()` (the `cd` preamble) now route through `quoteOneItem`.

3. src/main/java/org/codehaus/plexus/util/cli/Commandline.java:
   - Added `getLiteralExecutable()` (raw, unquoted) distinct from `getExecutable()` (shell-quoted, for shell-string callers).
   - `getCommandline()` (literal argv array used by `execute()`) and the position-tracking `Marker.getPosition()` now use `getLiteralExecutable()`.
   - `execute()` now calls `Runtime.getRuntime().exec(getCommandline(), environment, workingDir)` in both the "no working dir" and "with working dir" branches (previously called `Runtime.getRuntime().exec(getShellCommandline(), ...)`), so the actual subprocess is launched from a literal argv array instead of a single shell-interpreted command string. `getShellCommandline()` remains available for callers who explicitly need shell semantics.
   - `verifyShellState()` checks `shell.getOriginalExecutable() == null` instead of `shell.getExecutable() == null` (avoids triggering shell-quoting logic as a side effect of a null check).

4. Tests: ported the corresponding upstream test-expectation updates in `BourneShellTest.java` and `CommandlineTest.java` (quoting output changed from conditional double-quoting to unconditional single-quoting), and added two new regression tests in `CommandlineTest.java`:
   - `testPathWithShellExpansionStrings` (from upstream): executable path containing `$` must not trigger shell expansion.
   - `testExecutableWithShellMetacharactersIsNotInjected` (new, project-specific): sets `Commandline.setExecutable()` to a string containing a backtick command-substitution payload (`.../doesnotexist\`touch <marker>\``) and asserts (a) the process launch fails because no file literally named that exists, and (b) the marker file is never created — i.e., the backticks are never handed to a shell for interpretation. Verified this test fails against the pre-patch code (marker file created / no exception) and passes post-patch.

All 283 pre-existing tests plus the 2 new tests pass (285/285), and `mvn -B -DskipTests package` builds cleanly.
parsed_output.risk_notes: This is a behavior-changing security fix, not just a spot patch: (1) BourneShell now unconditionally single-quotes every executable/argument/working-directory string it builds, so `Shell.getShellCommandLine()`/`getCommandLine()` output differs from before for all Unix-shell users (any code that string-matches or parses that output, rather than treating it as an opaque command line for `/bin/sh -c`, will need updating — none exists in this repo's own callers). (2) `Commandline.execute()` no longer executes via `/bin/sh -c \"<shell-quoted string>\"`; it now execs the literal argv array via `Runtime.exec(String[], String[], File)` even when no working directory was set. This means any caller that relied on real shell features (globbing, pipes, `&&`, env-var expansion, `~` expansion) inside a single executable/argument string via `Commandline.execute()` will no longer get shell interpretation — this is intentional (it's the injection surface being removed) but is a functional behavior change consumers should be aware of. `getShellCommandline()` itself is preserved unchanged in shape for callers who explicitly want a shell-ready string/array (e.g. to hand to their own `ProcessBuilder`/shell invocation) — only the internal `execute()` path was switched away from it. CmdShell/CommandShell (Windows) quoting behavior is untouched, matching the actual upstream fix scope (upstream did not change CmdShell either). Recommend a full downstream regression pass (Maven plugins etc. that depend on plexus-utils Commandline) before upgrading, consistent with how the real CVE fix was released as a minor version bump.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed CWE-078 OS command injection in plexus-utils' Commandline/Shell machinery (this repo is plexus-utils 3.0.15, vulnerable to CVE-2022-4244-class shell injection, fixed upstream in commit b38a1b3a43 "[PLXUTILS-161] Commandline shell injection problems"). Root cause: BourneShell double-quoted the executable/working-directory when it needed quoting (`"..."`), but only escaped the quote character itself, not `$`, backtick, or `\` — so an attacker-controlled executable string like `foo`touch /tmp/pwned`bar` was wrapped as `"foo`touch /tmp/pwned`bar"` and the shell still performed backtick command substitution inside the double quotes. Additionally, `Commandline.execute()` always funneled execution through the shell-quoted single-string command line (`getShellCommandline()` -> `/bin/sh -c "..."`), so any gap in the quoting logic was directly exploitable via `Runtime.exec()`. I ported the verified upstream fix: BourneShell now unconditionally wraps every executable/argument/working-directory token in single quotes and embeds any literal single quote via the standard POSIX `'"'"'` technique (single-quoted content is fully inert to `$`, backticks, and backslashes in POSIX shells, closing the injection). `Shell`/`Commandline` were updated in lockstep (`quoteOneItem`, `setUnconditionalQuoting`, `getOriginalExecutable`, `getLiteralExecutable`) and `Commandline.execute()` now calls `Runtime.exec(getCommandline(), env, workingDir)` — a literal argv array — instead of building and re-interpreting a shell command string, removing the shell string-construction attack surface from the primary execution path entirely (CmdShell/Windows and getShellCommandline() are unaffected/preserved for callers who still need shell semantics explicitly). Verified by reproducing the injection pre-patch (backtick payload in `executable` created a marker file) and confirming it no longer executes post-patch; all 283 pre-existing tests plus 2 new regression tests pass, and `mvn -B -DskipTests package` succeeds.
